title: Teluni
html:
Teluni is a planned multi-tenant digital signage SaaS built on the Orion engineering foundation. It will let companies centrally manage images, videos, playlists and schedules on displays, with reliable offline playback. Brazil is the initial market, with international use anticipated. The core is intended for multiple business segments, from a single shop to a branch network.

Every screen. One place. · Todas as suas telas. Um só lugar.

Start with the product documentation for the vision, MVP acceptance criteria, proposed architecture, risks and delivery phases. The name Teluni and principal domain teluni.app are approved; branding records the defensive teluni.com.br option, current exclusion of teluni.com, and proposed visual identities. Final asset approval, domain registration/control evidence, trademark outcome and commercial pricing remain pending.

Current state

This repository was initialized on 2026-10-17 from Orion commit 53bcc705a9f68f01aa1bbea3a0f4df4a009577ea. It contains the foundation's architecture, policies, accepted ADRs, tooling, validation gate, CI, generated references, and Living Documentation Portal, and no product modules yet: the API serves only health endpoints, and the web application shows its shell and the portal. A concrete authentication provider and production environment have not been selected.

The project plan and project human actions own this repository's current work and external prerequisites. The project manifest records the project identity, the immutable initialization commit, and the Orion baseline currently integrated. Project derivation explains how to inspect provenance and adopt newer Orion revisions through reviewed merges.

The initial product brief is documented. Tenant workflows, media/programming/publication modules, the Android TV player, and production deployment remain unimplemented. The product architecture and ADR-0018 through ADR-0021 are proposals for review; this documentation does not authorize their implementation.

Accepted architecture and implemented capability are different states. Consult the technology map for selected directions and deliberately deferred choices, and validation availability for current checks. With Node.js 24.13.0 and pnpm 11.25.0, follow the canonical development setup for installation, local environment loading, execution, and the full gate.

Directory trees in architecture documents describe intended responsibilities, not proof that those directories exist. The physical repository takes precedence over illustrations. English is the canonical repository language; product localization is separate.
